{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The United States has a growing “care deficit” as the number of people who need care has grown.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Americans work, on average, 160 hours per year longer in the formal labor market than they did 30 years ago.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The United States ranks 168th out of 173 countries surveyed in regards to guaranteed paid parental leave, alongside Lesotho and Swaziland.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The United States ranks 146th in mandated paid sick days for short or long-term illness.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The United States fails to legislate a maximum length for the workweek, unlike 134 other countries.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The United States uniquely makes caring for one’s loved ones primarily a private burden among advanced democratic nations.",
"claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Northern and Western European nations use policies that include high-quality public day care and preschool.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Northern and Western European nations use policies that include paid maternity and paternity leave.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Northern and Western European nations have initiated child allowances to enable working families to better afford the costs of raising children.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Northern and Western European health and social insurance systems enable a high proportion of the dependent elderly to afford dignified, professional, in-home care.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
